title: Proteomic evaluation and comparison of native and decellularized human saphenous vein extracellular matrices
projectDescription: This project presents a label-free quantitative proteomic analysis of human saphenous vein (hSV) before and after decellularization, i.e. removal of cellular material using a CHAPS-based protocol. The study evaluated extracellular matrix preservation, vascular basement membrane composition changes, and residual cellular proteins, with protein classifications performed using MatrisomeDB and Gene Ontology annotation. The data provide a reference framework for assessing the impact of decellularization on hSV grafting material and its protein composition.
sampleProcessingProtocol: For proteomic profiling, 10 samples were prepared from native and their decellularized counterparts, in duplicates with a three-step lysis protocol. Frozen samples were first pulverized in a mortar with a pestle in liquid nitrogen, followed by 40min incubation with 200μm radioimmunoprecipitation assay (RIPA) lysis buffer supplemented with 1x HALT protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail (Thermo Fischer Scientific) in ice with gentle mixing with a pipette and then centrifuged at 8000x g for 10min. The supernatants were pipetted to new 1.5mL Eppendorf tubes and kept on ice. The remaining insoluble fraction from the samples were lysed again in 200μl of 7M UREA and 2M thiourea buffer supplemented with 5% CHAPS, 1mM EDTA and 1x HALT in 30mM Tris-HCl buffer, pH 8.5 for 40min in RT and similarly mixed gently during the incubation and then centrifuged. The supernatant from the second lysis step was added to the RIPA lysate and gently mixed and kept in ice. The total protein in the samples was measured with Bio-Rad Protein Assay (Bio-Rad Laboratories Inc., Hercules, CA, USA) according to manufacturer’s Microtiter Plate Protocol and absorbance was measured at 595nm with Victor™ X5.25µg of protein from all lysates were precipitated with 70% acetonitrile onto magnetic beads (MagReSynAmine, Resyn Biosciences). The proteins were washed on the beads with 100% acetonitrile, 70% ethanol and then resuspended in 50µl 50mM ammoniumbicarbonate containing 10mM DTT for reduction of cysteines. Samples were incubated at 37oC for 60 min. Then, to alkylate proteins, 50 µl of 30mM IAA in 50mM ammonium bicarbonate was added and samples were incubated at RT in the dark for 30 minutes. 1 µg trypsin was added to each sample for overnight on-beads protein digestion at 37°C. The resulting peptides were desalted on C18 stage tips (Affinisep) before LC-MS/MS analysis. The desalted peptide samples were analyzed by a nanoElute UHPLC coupled to a timsTOF fleX mass spectrometer (Bruker Daltonics, Bremen, Germany) via a CaptiveSpray ion source. Peptides were separated on a 25cm reversed-phase C18 column (1.6µm bead size, 120Å pore size, 75µm inner diameter, Ion Optics) with a flow rate of 0.3µl/min and a solvent gradient from 0-35% B in 60 minutes. Solvent B was 100% acetonitrile in 0.1% formic acid and solvent A 0.1% formic acid in water. The mass spectrometer was operated in data-dependent Parallel Accumulation-Serial Fragmentation (PASEF) mode. Mass spectra for MS and MS/MS scans were recorded between m/z 100 and 1700. Ion mobility resolution was set to 0.35–0.85 V·s/cm over a ramp time of 100 ms. Data-dependent acquisition was performed using 10 PASEF MS/MS scans per cycle with a near 100% duty cycle. A polygon filter was applied in the m/z and ion mobility space to exclude low m/z, singly charged ions from PASEF precursor selection. An active exclusion time of 0.4 min was applied to precursors that reached 20 000 intensity units. Collisional energy was ramped stepwise as a function of ion mobility.
dataProcessingProtocol: MS raw files were submitted to MaxQuant software (version 2.0.1.0)(Cox and Mann, 2008) for protein identification and quantification. Parameters were set as follows: carbamidomethylation as fixed modification and protein N-acetylation and methionine oxidation as variable modifications. First search error window of 20 ppm and mains search error of 4.5 ppm. Trypsin without proline restriction enzyme option was used, with two allowed miscleavages. Minimal unique peptides were set to 1, and FDR allowed was 0.01 (1%) for peptide and protein identification. Option ‘match between run’ (MBR) was used. The Uniprot human database was used (download from Uniprot Sept. 2020). Generation of reversed sequences was selected to assign FDR rates.  LC-MS/MS files from technical duplicates were combined in MaxQuant search.
